title: Scrolling a tall menu is opted into site by site, and the contents sidebar's menu was missed
why: At the head (46ca028) six sites wrap their contents in chrome::scrolled and outline/mod.rs:163 does not. A chrome::show_popup helper removes the repetition, but it does not make chrome the only caller of Popup::show: nothing stops a new site calling egui directly, and the lint that would (clippy disallowed-methods) is a new clippy.toml entry, which rule 3 forbids. The outline menu gaining the wrapper is reader-visible in a window too short for it.
observable: In a very short window the contents sidebar's menu would scroll instead of running off the window.
size: 6 files, about 25 lines, 6 call sites (the SubMenu site keeps calling scrolled)
guards: tests/reader/menu_room.rs (POPUPS table: add the contents menu), sidebars::the_menu_shows_and_switches_the_contents_sidebar, popover.rs, tabs*.rs. Popup<'a>'s lifetime in the helper needs a compile.

options.name: Add show_popup, use it at every Popup site and wrap the outline menu
options.cost: About 25 lines in 6 files and one more row in the menu_room test; the outline menu scrolls in a short window.

options.name: Wrap only the outline menu
options.cost: One line and one test row; the opt-in stays as it is.

options.name: Leave it
options.cost: Nothing; the two-row outline menu is the one popup that cannot scroll.

title: The zoom row keeps itself in view with its own per-frame memory and a frame-number check
why: The code is as quoted (overflow_menu/mod.rs:248-264). The reviewer's doubt is settled: a menu scrolled, closed and opened again opens at its old offset, not at its top, so the comment 'a menu opened again at another zoom starts from its top' is false. The frame check is still needed for another reason: without it a menu reopened at another zoom would scroll to the zoom row on opening. So move the rule into chrome as proposed, keep the frame number, and correct the comment.
observable: none if moved as it is
diff:
sketch, not compiled
- fn keep_in_view_through_a_zoom(ui: &egui::Ui) { .. }   // overflow_menu
+ pub(super) fn stays_in_view_through_a_rescale(ui: &egui::Ui) { .. }   // chrome, beside show_what_gained_the_keyboard
- // The frame before this one: a menu opened again at another zoom
- // starts from its top.
+ // Only while the menu stays open: one opened again keeps the place it
+ // was scrolled to, and must not jump to this row.
guards: tests/reader/menu_room.rs the_zoom_row_stays_in_reach_when_zooming_makes_the_menu_scroll, popover.rs the_zoom_row_of_the_menu_stays_open_while_it_is_pressed. No test covers reopening.
repro: reproduced: `REOPEN same zoom: top 20.019531 scrolled -218.01758 again -218.01758` (New Tab's top before scrolling, after, and after close and reopen)

options.name: Move it into chrome, keep the frame check, fix the comment
options.cost: About 25 lines moved, no behaviour change.

options.name: Move it and drop the frame check
options.cost: 3 lines fewer; a menu reopened after a zoom then jumps to the zoom row.

options.name: Leave it in overflow_menu and fix only the comment
options.cost: 2 lines; the rule stays out of reach of the other popups.

title: New: a menu that was scrolled opens again where it was left, not at its top
why: Not in the review, found while settling 28-F2. egui keeps a ScrollArea's offset by id and chrome::scrolled never resets it (chrome/mod.rs:110-131), so the More menu scrolled to Quit, closed with Escape and opened again shows its end, with New Tab out of view. It only shows in a window too short for the menu.
observable: A reopened menu starts scrolled to where it was last left.
size: 1 file, about 8 lines, one reader test
guards: None today ('Nothing tests the reopen-from-top claim', as the review says).
repro: reproduced: `REOPEN same zoom: top 20.019531 scrolled -218.01758 again -218.01758`

options.name: Reset the offset when a popup opens
options.cost: About 8 lines and a test; shares the opened-this-frame test with 28-F2.

options.name: Keep the offset and say so in the comment
options.cost: A comment; some readers will take a menu that opens at its end for a bug.

title: scrolled states the height limit twice
why: ui.set_max_height(room) (chrome/mod.rs:119) already bounds what the ScrollArea may take: egui's ScrollArea::show sizes itself as available.at_most(max_size) (scroll_area.rs:717-719 of egui 0.33), so .max_height(room) at :123 adds nothing. popup_room has one caller and can fold in.
size: 1 file, 1 line (and popup_room folded in: about 8 lines, with 28-T1)
guards: tests/reader/menu_room.rs, all of it; a_menu_that_scrolls_stands_clear_of_the_top_and_the_bottom_of_the_window pins the room.

title: The Aa popover was wrapped by nesting three closures
why: appearance/mod.rs:112-133: show, scrolled and Frame::show each open a closure. Extracting the sections as the More menu's rows were takes one level out; 28-F1's helper takes another.
guards: tests/reader/popover.rs. The TSV row on src/app/appearance/mod.rs replaces other text.

title: A unit test restates a private subtraction
why: a_popup_has_the_height_of_the_window_less_its_frame_and_the_air_around_it (chrome/tests.rs:597-600) checks popup_room(800, 14) == 778. The reader test on the menu's clearance from the top and bottom of the window covers the same rule from outside.
